dataset.title: Results
dataset.description: One row per page. status is OK when the row carries a real measurement, or NOT_CHECKED_* with the reason in plain words: INVALID (the line is not an http url), DUPLICATE (the same url came earlier), LIMIT (beyond maxPages), PRIVATE_ADDRESS (a host name really answered with a non public address, whether the page host, a redirect hop or a subresource; a redirect and a subresource are recognised after the load and such a row is never charged, while a subresource host that does not resolve at all is not a private address and does not block the page), DNS_ERROR (the host name does not resolve or is not a valid host name), TIMEOUT (the page did not finish loading in pageTimeoutSecs), HTTP_ERROR (the page answered 4xx or 5xx), NOT_HTML (the response is a pdf, an image or anything else that is not a page), PROBE_ERROR (Chromium could not measure the page), TIME, CAP, BILLING and ERROR (the run stopped before this page for the reason in the summary). lcpMs, cls, tbtMs, ttfbMs and fcpMs are the lab measurements; ratings carries good, needs-improvement or poor for each of them by Google's published thresholds, and verdict is the worst of those ratings. tbtMs is total blocking time, a lab proxy for INP: INP itself is a field metric and is not reported here at all. transferBytes is a floor, not the real weight, because a cross origin resource without Timing-Allow-Origin reports zero bytes, and bytesPartial says when that happened. redirects lists the urls the browser went through, so a page that pays for a redirect chain is visible. resourceHosts lists at most 25 subresource host names, resourceHostsTotal is how many were seen and resourceHostsTruncated says the list was cut. billable is true only on a row that carries a measurement; the money actually taken is in the run summary.

summary.title: Run summary
summary.description: Run summary. requested is how many lines were sent, blank lines included; processed plus notChecked always equals requested. delivered counts OK rows, rowsWritten counts every row written, chargedEvents is what the platform charged, billingActive says whether this run could bill at all. chargedEvents and delivered are the same number unless a charge failed: deliveredUncharged counts those rows and chargeErrors the attempts, writeErrors counts rows the dataset refused. stopReason is null, spending-cap, charge-error, dataset-write-error, deadline, billing-price-unknown or unexpected-error, and unexpectedError carries the reason for the last one. byStatus is the full breakdown and byVerdict counts good, needs-improvement and poor pages. cutByMaxPages is the tail the limit cut and maxPages the limit actually applied. privateBlocked counts every page the address guard stopped, privateSubresourceBlocked the part of it that came from a subresource, dnsErrors the host names that did not resolve, subresourceDnsSkipped the subresource names that did not resolve at all and so blocked nothing, pagesWithTruncatedHostList the pages whose subresource host list was cut at 25 names, subresourceHostLookups how many subresource names the address guard resolved; httpErrors, notHtml, timeouts and probeErrors count the other free rows by cause. pageMarginSecs is the margin the deadline check used. rowsWritten counts the rows handed to the dataset, and a row whose charge failed counts in deliveredUncharged because one SDK call writes the row before it charges. strategy is the device profile used. datasetItemCount is our own count of written rows, datasetItemCountApi the same as the platform reported it, datasetItemCountNote explains a gap. The named store keeps one object per run under RUN_SUMMARY-<runId>.
